problem.heading: Why most marketers are AI stuck

cards.title: Generic learning
cards.body: You've watched the YouTube videos, read the LinkedIn posts, even taken a course or two. But you still don't have a single AI tool in production.
cards.answer: We give you actionable workflows you can ship tomorrow morning.

cards.title: Building in isolation
cards.body: Your company has one person figuring out AI, and it's you. Nobody to tell you your approach is wrong before you spend a week on it. Here, someone will tell you in an afternoon.
cards.answer: Experience a community of builders who share what works, what doesn't, and what's next.

cards.title: The "technical" gap
cards.body: Most training is either "too basic" (surface-level prompting) or "too hard" (complex engineering). Neither helps you do your actual job better.
cards.answer: We bridge the gap: powerful AI tools explained in plain marketing language.

steps.heading: Your first week in the lab

items.title: 👋 Introduce yourself
items.html: Tell people what you're trying to build and what's in your way. 81 members have.

items.title: 🧪 Pick your first experiment
items.html: Steal a workflow from the library (65 and counting) or bring the half-built idea sitting in your drafts.

items.title: 🚀 Ship it at the next session
items.html: Get unstuck live with the group, then post what you made in Share Your Wins. 42 people have gone before you.

cards.title: Hackathon sessions
cards.html: Stop struggling alone. Bring your unfinished AI projects and get unstuck in real-time. What takes weeks to solve solo, we solve together in 90 minutes. Eight member hackathons run so far.

cards.title: Hands-on AI implementation
cards.html: We don't do passive webinars. These are working sessions where you open your laptop, follow along, and leave with a finished asset, not just more notes. Recent ones: build your first MCP in 30 minutes, Claude Code in terminal, local LLMs, Git and GitHub, required statistics for marketers.

cards.title: A network of AI builders
cards.html: Trade ideas with marketers who are actually using AI, not just talking about it. A safe space to share failures, experiments, and wins without judgment.

cards.title: The "Steal This" library
cards.html: Don't start from scratch. 65 tutorials, prompts, Python scripts, and workflows, from vector embeddings and internal linking to building your first MCP. All with the code.

cards.title: The job board
cards.html: Updated regularly, with 90+ AI and marketing roles posted so far. Listings that include salary get priority, so you're not guessing what it pays. Recent ones ran $120k to $275k at Postman, JPMorgan Chase, Houzz, and Modern Treasury. Filled roles come down, so what's on the board is what's open.

pullQuote.text: I've spent over a decade inside the ML and AI world, watching how quietly it's designed to exclude: academically, financially, geographically, linguistically.

founder.heading: A decade inside AI. Explained in plain marketing language.
founder.photoAlt: Britney Muller, founder of Orange Labs
paragraphs: I've spent over a decade inside the ML and AI world, watching how quietly it's designed to exclude: academically, financially, geographically, linguistically. Those barriers are unnecessary (and not a you problem). It's an industry problem.

Orange Labs started as a question from my students: "Where do we go from here?" I didn't have a great answer, so I built one. A place to ask anything, ship weird experiments, and stay connected to people who actually want you to succeed.

It's also become home for the resources, workshops, books, and advice I recommend most, gathered in one place instead of scattered across bookmarks and DMs, so they're easier for more people to actually find and use.

notForYou.heading: Not for you if
items: You want someone to build it for you
You want to be told AI will replace your job, or that it definitely won't
You're afraid to experiment, ship something messy, or get it wrong (totally normal, and exactly what we're here to help you push through)

items.q: I'm not technical. Will I keep up?
items.a: Orange Labs exists because most AI training is either too basic or too technical. Everything here is explained in plain marketing language, no CS degree required, ever.

items.q: How much time does this take?
items.a: As much or as little as you want. Biweekly "Quick AI Tips & Tricks" land in your inbox, and you can drop into the Lab whenever you need support or want to see what other members are building.

items.q: What if it's not for me?
items.a: Try it for 7 days risk-free and cancel any time. No waitlist, no lock-in, no hard feelings.

items.q: Isn't this just another community that goes quiet?
items.a: Fair question, and the honest answer is to go look. Every space shows the date of the last post. Take the seven free days, post the thing you're stuck on, and see what comes back. If it's dead in there, you've lost nothing.

items.q: I already use ChatGPT every day. What's different here?
items.a: Using ChatGPT is prompting. This is about what you build around it: connecting it to your real data, putting it on a schedule, wrapping it in something your team can actually use. Members here have shipped rank trackers, an ALT text generator that handled 27,000 images, and a fact checker that finds contradictions across a content set. Not prompts. Tools.

items.q: How is this different from your course?
items.a: The course is four weeks, cohort-based, with a syllabus and live classes. The community is ongoing, self-directed, and $49/mo. The course teaches you the foundations. The community is where you keep building after. You don't need one to join the other.
